entities.summary: Count Christian Günther von Bernstorff was a Danish and Prussian statesman and diplomat who played a significant role in the early 19th-century European politics. Born in Denmark around 1780, Bernstorff served as the Danish Minister in Prussia and later became the Prussian Minister of Foreign Affairs in 1807. He played a key role in negotiating the Treaty of Tilsit with Napoleon, which significantly impacted European politics and led to the reorganization of the continent. Bernstorff's diplomatic efforts helped to maintain the balance of power in Europe during the Napoleonic Wars, contributing to the eventual defeat of Napoleon in 1815. He was a member of the Prussian royal family and served as a senator in the Prussian Senate from 1820 until his death in 1835. Despite his significant contributions to European politics, Bernstorff's legacy is often overshadowed by his more prominent contemporaries, such as Napoleon and Tsar Alexander I. However, his diplomatic acumen and strategic thinking had a lasting impact on the development of European diplomacy and international relations.

entities.summary: Count Christian Günther von Bernstorff was a Danish and Prussian statesman and diplomat who played a crucial role in shaping European politics during the late 18th and early 19th centuries. Born in Copenhagen on April 3, 1769, von Bernstorff rose to prominence as a member of the Prussian government, where he served as the Minister of Foreign Affairs from 1811 to 1824. His diplomatic efforts helped to secure the Treaty of Kiel in 1814, which led to the establishment of the Duchy of Schleswig-Holstein and had significant implications for the balance of power in Europe. Von Bernstorff's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as his policies and alliances contributed to the unification of Germany under Prussian leadership. In the years following his death on March 28, 1835, von Bernstorff's reputation as a skilled diplomat and statesman continued to grow, cementing his place among the most influential figures of the period.
